summary:
The Monster Rice Rat (*Euryoryzomys lamia*) is a small mammal found only in the semi-deciduous forests and Cerrado woodlands of central Brazil — one of the most biodiverse and threatened ecosystems on Earth. Known from just a handful of scattered localities across Minas Gerais, Goiás, and the Federal District, this quiet, unassuming rodent carved out its existence in a landscape of rare beauty.

Its story is one shared by too many: forests cleared for agriculture, pasture, and logging have steadily erased its home. Two of its only four known locations have already been destroyed entirely. With its range shrinking and habitat quality declining, the Monster Rice Rat serves as a gentle reminder of what disappears when wildlands are lost — often before we ever truly knew them.
